name: Tinnitus
summary: Perception of ringing, buzzing, or similar noise without an external source.
notes: Commonly claimed after hazardous noise exposure. Usually assigned a single 10 percent evaluation regardless of whether one or both ears are affected.
rating_logic: 10%: recurrent tinnitus.
why_common: Frequent starter claim because veterans often report persistent ringing after service-related noise exposure.

name: Hearing Loss
summary: Reduced hearing acuity measured through controlled speech discrimination and puretone testing.
notes: Requires audiometric testing under VA rules. Often appears alongside tinnitus and noise exposure claims.
rating_logic: Rated mechanically from Maryland CNC speech discrimination scores and puretone threshold averages.
evidence_checklist: Functional impact on conversation or work
why_common: Often paired with tinnitus and occupational noise exposure patterns.

name: Vertigo / Dizziness
summary: Episodes of dizziness or spinning sensation that may affect balance and mobility.
notes: Severity often depends on frequency, gait disturbance, and documented vestibular findings.
rating_logic: 10%: occasional dizziness.
30%: dizziness and occasional staggering.
evidence_checklist: Impact on driving, walking, or work
why_common: Often connected to ear-related claims and functional impact concerns.

name: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD)
summary: Trauma-related mental health condition evaluated under the general rating formula for mental disorders.
notes: Severity turns heavily on occupational and social impairment, symptom frequency, treatment history, and functional examples.
rating_logic: 0%, 10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 100% based on level of occupational and social impairment and symptom picture.
evidence_checklist: Diagnosis or mental health treatment records
Symptoms such as nightmares, hypervigilance, avoidance, panic, or mood changes
Examples of occupational and social impact
why_common: One of the most common VA claim paths and often connects to sleep, headache, and functioning issues.

name: Anxiety Disorder
summary: Persistent anxiety symptoms rated under the general mental disorders formula.
notes: Like other mental health ratings, the key issue is functional impairment rather than a simple symptom count.
rating_logic: 0%, 10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 100% based on occupational and social impairment.
evidence_checklist: Mental health diagnosis or treatment records
Examples of work and relationship impact
why_common: Common standalone claim and also often appears alongside sleep or headache complaints.

name: Depressive Disorder
summary: Depressive symptoms rated under the general mental disorders formula.
notes: Evidence is strongest when it shows mood symptoms plus concrete work, motivation, concentration, or relationship effects.
rating_logic: 0%, 10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 100% based on occupational and social impairment.
evidence_checklist: Low mood, motivation, isolation, or concentration problems
why_common: Frequently claimed directly or alongside other chronic service-connected problems.

name: Insomnia / Chronic Sleep Impairment
summary: Persistent sleep disturbance that often appears within mental health evaluations or as part of related symptom patterns.
notes: Sleep impairment often matters as severity/support evidence even when not separately rated.
rating_logic: Typically evaluated under the general mental disorders formula when service connected as a mental health condition.
evidence_checklist: Sleep onset or sleep maintenance problems
Treatment attempts or sleep hygiene notes
why_common: Very common supporting issue in mental health and chronic pain claim patterns.

name: Adjustment Disorder
summary: Stress-related mental health condition rated under the general mental disorders formula.
notes: The rating focus is still occupational and social impairment, not just the diagnosis label.
rating_logic: 0%, 10%, 30%, 50%, 70%, 100% based on occupational and social impairment.
why_common: Shows up often when symptoms are documented but diagnostic labels vary across providers.

name: Migraines
summary: Headache condition where rating often turns on frequency, severity, and economic impact.
notes: Prostrating attacks and the effect on work are especially important.
rating_logic: 0%: less frequent attacks.
10%: characteristic prostrating attacks averaging one in 2 months over last several months.
30%: characteristic prostrating attacks occurring on average once a month over last several months.
50%: very frequent completely prostrating and prolonged attacks productive of severe economic inadaptability.
why_common: A high-interest claim because rating turns on detailed symptom patterns the app can help organize.

name: Peripheral Neuropathy
summary: Nerve-related symptoms such as numbness, tingling, or pain often evaluated by affected nerve and severity.
notes: Needs clear identification of the affected extremity/nerve and the degree of impairment.
rating_logic: Varies by nerve and whether impairment is mild, moderate, moderately severe, severe, or complete.
evidence_checklist: Functional impact like walking, standing, or hand use
why_common: Frequently appears as a secondary or associated neurological issue with spine claims.

name: Sciatica / Radiculopathy
summary: Radiating pain or nerve symptoms from the spine into the extremities, commonly rated by nerve severity.
notes: Often linked to lumbar or cervical spine conditions and needs side-specific functional evidence.
rating_logic: Varies by severity of incomplete paralysis or complete paralysis of the affected nerve.
evidence_checklist: Impact on standing, walking, sitting, or lifting
why_common: Very common secondary path from service-connected back or neck conditions.

name: Lumbar Strain / Low Back Condition
summary: Low back condition typically rated under the general rating formula for the spine.
notes: Range of motion, flare-ups, painful motion, and functional loss are central.
rating_logic: Generally rated based on thoracolumbar range of motion, guarding/spasm, ankylosis, and functional loss.
evidence_checklist: Pain with standing, walking, sitting, bending, or lifting
why_common: One of the most common orthopedic claims and often drives secondary pain-related issues.

name: Cervical Strain / Neck Condition
summary: Neck condition rated under the general rating formula for the spine.
notes: Range of motion, flare-ups, and associated upper-extremity nerve symptoms matter most.
rating_logic: Generally rated based on cervical range of motion, guarding/spasm, ankylosis, and functional loss.
evidence_checklist: Arm numbness, tingling, or weakness if present
why_common: Common orthopedic claim that often connects to headaches or upper-extremity symptoms.

name: Knee Limitation of Flexion
summary: Knee condition evaluated by limitation of flexion and functional loss.
notes: Painful motion, flare-ups, instability, and separate extension issues may all matter.
rating_logic: 0%, 10%, 20%, 30% depending on degree of limited flexion.
evidence_checklist: Instability, swelling, or locking if present
Impact on stairs, kneeling, squatting, standing, or walking
why_common: A very common claim area where detailed functional examples improve the record.

name: Knee Limitation of Extension
summary: Knee condition evaluated by limitation of extension and functional loss.
notes: Can sometimes be rated separately from limitation of flexion when supported.
rating_logic: 0%, 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50% depending on degree of limited extension.
evidence_checklist: Functional loss with walking, stairs, or standing
why_common: Often paired with other knee findings and useful in more complete orthopedic theories.

name: Shoulder Limitation of Motion
summary: Shoulder condition often rated by limitation of arm movement and functional loss.
notes: Dominant versus non-dominant arm may matter for percentages.
rating_logic: Percentages vary by whether motion is limited at shoulder level, midway, or to 25 degrees from side, and by dominant arm.
evidence_checklist: Functional loss at work or with daily tasks
why_common: A common motion-based orthopedic claim where concrete use limitations matter.

name: Ankle Limitation of Motion
summary: Ankle condition rated by severity of motion loss and functional impact.
notes: Pain with walking, standing, or uneven surfaces often strengthens severity evidence.
rating_logic: 10%: moderate limitation of motion.
20%: marked limitation of motion.
why_common: A frequent lower-extremity claim with clear functional examples.

name: Plantar Fasciitis
summary: Foot condition often involving heel or arch pain with standing and walking.
notes: Treatment response, orthotics, and whether symptoms remain despite treatment can matter.
rating_logic: 10%, 20%, 30% depending on unilateral/bilateral severity and response to treatment.
evidence_checklist: Functional impact on work or mobility
why_common: Very common functional pain claim, especially when standing and walking are limited.

name: Sleep Apnea
summary: Sleep-disordered breathing often evaluated by sleep study results and treatment needs.
notes: CPAP requirement is a major rating marker.
rating_logic: 0%: asymptomatic but documented sleep disorder breathing.
30%: persistent daytime hypersomnolence.
50%: requires use of breathing assistance device such as CPAP.
100%: chronic respiratory failure with carbon dioxide retention or cor pulmonale, or tracheostomy.
why_common: A frequent target for secondary theories and device-based rating discussions.

name: Asthma
summary: Respiratory condition rated using pulmonary function testing and treatment intensity.
notes: Frequency of attacks and steroid use can matter alongside PFTs.
rating_logic: Ratings vary by PFT results, frequency of exacerbations, physician visits, and steroid treatment.
why_common: Respiratory symptom claims often overlap with sinus and rhinitis evidence.

name: Sinusitis
summary: Sinus condition where rating often turns on episode frequency, antibiotic treatment, and symptoms like headaches or pain.
notes: Documentation of incapacitating or non-incapacitating episodes helps a lot.
rating_logic: 0%, 10%, 30%, 50% based on frequency and severity of episodes and surgical history.
why_common: Common upper-airway claim with good room for timeline and treatment evidence.

name: Rhinitis
summary: Nasal condition often rated based on obstruction and presence of polyps.
notes: Objective findings like obstruction or polyps are especially useful.
rating_logic: 10%: no polyps, but with greater than 50 percent obstruction of nasal passages on both sides or complete obstruction on one side.
30%: with polyps.
evidence_checklist: Functional symptoms like congestion or breathing disruption
why_common: Often paired with sinus and breathing complaints and common in presumptive discussions.

name: GERD / Reflux Symptoms
summary: Digestive symptoms such as reflux, regurgitation, or heartburn often evaluated by analogy.
notes: Severity evidence is stronger when it shows frequency, sleep disruption, diet impact, and medication use.
rating_logic: Often rated by analogy to hiatal hernia criteria based on symptom severity and health impairment.
evidence_checklist: Impact on overall health or daily functioning
why_common: A frequent chronic symptom claim, especially where medication and sleep impact are documented.

name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS)
summary: Digestive condition rated by severity of bowel disturbance and abdominal distress.
notes: Frequency and severity details matter more than a short label alone.
rating_logic: 0%: mild.
10%: moderate; frequent episodes of bowel disturbance with abdominal distress.
30%: severe; diarrhea, or alternating diarrhea and constipation, with more or less constant abdominal distress.
why_common: Often benefits from a strong symptom log and is common in chronic stress-related claim patterns.

name: Hypertension
summary: High blood pressure claim typically evaluated by predominantly elevated readings and medication history.
notes: Longitudinal blood pressure evidence helps more than isolated readings.
rating_logic: 10%, 20%, 40%, 60% based on predominantly elevated systolic/diastolic readings and medication history.
evidence_checklist: Any secondary relationship theory if applicable
why_common: Often appears in chronic-condition reviews and benefits from organized longitudinal readings.

name: Erectile Dysfunction
summary: Condition often raised as a secondary issue related to mental health, medication, or other service-connected conditions.
notes: Often important for secondary theory and special monthly compensation discussions.
rating_logic: May involve schedular criteria plus consideration of SMC depending on facts.
why_common: A frequent secondary issue tied to medication side effects and chronic-condition theories.

name: Painful or Unstable Scars
summary: Scar claims often turn on pain, instability, size, and number of scars.
notes: Photos and descriptions of pain or instability can be helpful.
rating_logic: 10%, 20%, 30% based on number of painful or unstable scars, with possible additional considerations.
why_common: A common residual issue where good descriptive evidence can quickly strengthen the file.
